ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $C$ is a point on $\odot O$. The bisector of $\angle OCB$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $D$. A tangent to $\odot O$ at point $D$ intersects the extension of line $CB$ at point $E$. $CE \perp DE$; if $AB=10$, and $\tan A= \frac{1}{3}$, find the length of $DE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $OD\parallel CE$,\\
it follows that $\angle ODC=\angle DCE$.\\
Given $OD=OA$ and $OC=OD$,\\
it implies $\angle A=\angle ADO$ and $\angle ODC=\angle OCD$.\\
Since $\angle A=\angle DCE$,\\
we have $\angle A=\angle OCD=\angle ADO=\angle CDO$.\\
Given $OA=OC$,\\
it results in $\triangle ADO\cong \triangle CDO$ (AAS),\\
thus, $CD=AD$.\\
Since $AB$ is the diameter, we have $\angle ADB=90^\circ$,\\
and given $\tan A=\frac{DB}{AD}=\frac{1}{3}$ and $AB=10$,\\
from $AD^2+DB^2=AB^2=100$\\
we find $BD=\sqrt{10}$, $AD=3\sqrt{10}$,\\
thus, $CD=AD=3\sqrt{10}$.\\
Since $\angle A=\angle DCE$ and $\angle ADB=\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
$\triangle ADB\sim \triangle CED$,\\
it follows that $\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac{BD}{DE}$,\\
thus, $\frac{10}{3\sqrt{10}}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{DE}$,\\
resulting in $DE=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle centered at O, AB is a horizontal diameter, A is at the left end of the circle, and B is at the right end of the circle. C is on the lower circumference of the circle, and D is on the upper-right circumference. Line segment CD connects from C to D and is indicated as the angle bisector of ∠OCB. Through D, draw tangent DE to the circle; E is located to the right of B and on the extension of CB; in the figure CE is perpendicular to DE. Reasoning: Because DE is the tangent to the circle at point D, OD ⟂ DE; and it is known that CE ⟂ DE, therefore OD ∥ CE. From OD ∥ CE, it follows that ∠ODC = ∠DCE. Also because C, B, E are collinear, and CD bisects ∠OCB, ∠OCD = ∠DCB = ∠DCE. On the other hand, ∠DAB and ∠DCB are both inscribed angles subtending the same arc DB, so ∠A = ∠DCE. Since OA, OC, OD are all radii, OA = OC = OD; in △AOD, OA = OD, so ∠A = ∠ADO. Combining the above angle relationships, △AOD and △COD have equal corresponding angles, and OA = OC, therefore AD = CD can be obtained. Because AB is a diameter and D is on the circle, ∠ADB = 90°. In right triangle ADB, tan A = BD/AD = 1/3; let BD = x, then AD = 3x. Also AB = 10, so AD^2 + BD^2 = AB^2, that is (3x)^2 + x^2 = 100, obtaining 10x^2 = 100, x = √10. Therefore BD = √10, AD = 3√10. From AD = CD, get CD = 3√10. In right triangle CDE, ∠E = 90°, and ∠DCE = ∠A. From △ADB we know sin A = BD/AB = √10/10 = 1/√10. Therefore DE = CD · sin∠DCE = 3√10 · 1/√10 = 3.
